ex.s: When attending an event at SoFi Stadium, you’re just a short walk or ride from several comfortable and classy hotels.

ex.s: If you’re willing to drive a little further, the Ritz-Carlton Los Angeles promises luxurious rooms and extensive leisure facilities — perfect for turning a game day into a great weekend escape.

ex.s: Not long ago, my fifth-grade son Kevin asked me about the meaning of a word in a novel.
ex.t: 不久前，我上五年级的儿子凯文问我一本小说里一个词的意思。

ex.s: Suddenly it occurred to me that he did not even know how to use a dictionary.
ex.t: 我突然意识到，他甚至不知道该怎么用词典。

ex.s: I took down one of the dictionaries, and we read it together for a few minutes before I handed it to him.
ex.t: 我取下一本词典，和他一起读了几分钟，然后把它交给了他。

ex.s: It took him a few tries to find the word in question.
ex.t: 他试了好几次才找到要查的那个词。

ex.s: While going through the pages, he kept saying, wide-eyed: “How can there be this many words?” After a while, he looked at me and asked, “Do you know all these words, Mom?” I smiled, “I definitely do not know all these words,” I said.
ex.t: 翻页的时候，他睁大眼睛不停地说：“怎么会有这么多词？”过了一会儿，他看着我问：“妈妈，这些词你都认识吗？”我笑了笑说：“我当然不可能全都认识。”

ex.s: I had my first dictionary as a gift for my 13th birthday.
ex.t: 我的第一本词典是13岁生日时收到的礼物。

ex.s: I felt a small pain in my chest The dictionary was stolen at the end of my freshman year of college.
ex.t: 我胸口隐隐作痛——那本词典在我大一结束时被偷了。

ex.s: What does Kevin usually do to get the meaning of a word?
ex.t: 凯文通常用什么方法来了解一个词的意思？

ex.s: It was given to Kevin as a gift.
ex.t: 它被作为礼物送给了凯文。

ex.s: It was a valuable limited edition.
ex.t: 它是很有价值的限量版。

ex.s: Dictionaries are still a useful tool.
ex.t: 词典仍然是有用的工具。

ex.s: They provide shade, lower surface temperatures, absorb a surprising amount of airborne carbon, remove tiny pollutants, and provide wildlife habitat along with just plain beauty.
ex.t: 它们提供树荫、降低地表温度、吸收空气中惊人数量的碳、去除微小污染物，还为野生动物提供栖息地，并带来纯粹的美感。

ex.s: Something could go wrong, though, according to a new study.
ex.t: 不过，一项新研究指出，事情也可能出问题。

ex.s: Oaks and sweetgums, which currently account for a majority of the city’s trees, produce huge amounts of a chemical substance called isoprene.
ex.t: 橡树和枫香树目前占纽约市树木的大多数，它们会产生大量一种叫作异戊二烯的化学物质。

ex.s: A study carried out by some of its researchers several years ago concluded that city trees did release isoprene.
ex.t: 该局一些研究人员几年前开展的一项研究得出结论：城市树木确实会释放异戊二烯。

ex.s: “We didn’t make a big deal of that,” said Novem Auyeung, a Parks Department senior scientist.
ex.t: “我们当时没有把这事看得太重，”公园管理局资深科学家Novem Auyeung说。

ex.s: Suspending tree-planting for a few decades.
ex.t: 暂停植树几十年。

ex.s: In the study, 187 people were invited to visit Kettle’s Yard gallery during an exhibition of handmade clay objects.
ex.t: 在这项研究中，187人受邀在手工陶艺品展览期间参观了Kettle's Yard美术馆。

ex.s: Participants were randomly divided into two groups: the “beauty” group was asked to actively consider and then rate the beauty of each object they viewed, while the control group just matched a line drawing of the object with the artwork itself.
ex.t: 参与者被随机分成两组：“美感”组被要求主动思考并评价每件所见物品的美，而对照组只是把物品的线描图与艺术品本身进行匹配。

ex.s: All participants were then tested on how they process information, and whether it's in a more practical or abstract way.
ex.t: 随后，所有参与者都接受了信息处理方式测试，以判断他们的思维方式更偏向实际还是抽象。

ex.s: While they were told the study was about cognitive processes, participants were asked about interests, with around half saying they had an artistic hobby.
ex.t: 虽然参与者被告知该研究是关于认知过程的，但他们也被问及兴趣爱好，约一半人说自己有艺术爱好。

ex.s: Among those, the effect was greater: those with an artistic hobby in the beauty group scored over 25% higher on average for abstract thinking than those with an artistic hobby in the control group.
ex.t: 在这些人中，效果更明显：美感组中有艺术爱好的人，其抽象思维平均得分比对照组中有艺术爱好的人高出25%以上。

ex.s: Across all participants, those in the beauty group reported an average of 23% higher levels of “transformative and self-transcendent feelings” — such as feeling moved, enlightened and inspired — than the control group.
ex.t: 在所有参与者中，美感组报告的“蜕变性和超越自我的感受”——如感动、受启迪、受鼓舞——平均比对照组高出23%。

ex.s: “We usually think in very concrete terms when doing something on a screen,” said Simone Schnall, senior author of the study.
ex.t: “我们在屏幕上做事时，通常以非常具体的方式思考，”该研究的资深作者Simone Schnall说。

ex.s: Emily Sanders, a 25-year-old from Detroit, Michigan, set out on December 23rd with high hopes of reaching Toronto to meet her boyfriend for Christmas.
ex.t: 25岁的Emily Sanders来自密歇根州底特律，12月23日她满怀希望地出发，打算赶到多伦多与男友共度圣诞节。

ex.s: Although she had heard warnings about an approaching snowstorm, she didn’t give it much thought.
ex.t: 尽管她听说过即将到来的暴风雪警告，但并没有太当回事。

ex.s: She drove on for a while and found herself on an unfamiliar road toward a Canadian town.
ex.t: 她又开了一会儿，发现自己行驶在一条通往加拿大小镇的陌生道路上。

ex.s: After a struggle, she managed to free the vehicle and continued inching along the snow-covered road.
ex.t: 经过一番努力，她设法把车弄了出来，继续在积雪覆盖的道路上缓慢前行。

ex.s: While Emily was driving on a narrow stretch of road, her car slid into a ditch (沟).
ex.t: 当Emily行驶在一段狭窄的路上时，她的车滑进了沟里。

ex.s: She wrapped herself in a blanket, waiting for morning.
ex.t: 她裹上毯子，等待天亮。

ex.s: Emily awoke to a gentle knock on her car window.
ex.t: Emily被轻轻的敲车窗声唤醒。

ex.s: With genuine warmth in her voice, Rachel said they could take Emily to a nearby cafe they knew.
ex.t: Rachel的声音里带着真诚的温暖，她说他们可以带Emily去一家他们熟悉的附近咖啡馆。

ex.s: In the cafe, the couple bought Emily a hot chocolate and listened patiently as she explained her desperate situation: she was about a hundred miles from her destination, her car was completely stuck, and her entire holiday plan could be ruined.
ex.t: 在咖啡馆里，这对夫妇给Emily买了一杯热巧克力，耐心地听她讲述自己的绝境：她离目的地大约还有一百英里，车完全陷住了，整个假期计划可能都要泡汤。

ex.s: But elevation is necessarily relative: only the choice of a reference point allows us to express numerically the height of an object or a location.
ex.t: 但海拔必然是相对的：只有选定一个参照点，我们才能用数字表示一个物体或地点的高度。

ex.s: The idea of sea level as a reference point for elevations has by now been around for so long as to go essentially unnoticed-we mention it without even considering what it means.
ex.t: 以海平面作为海拔参照点的想法由来已久，以至于人们基本不再留意——我们提到它时甚至不会去想它意味着什么。

ex.s: That the concept has a history is easily ignored.
ex.t: 这个概念也有其历史，这一点很容易被忽视。

ex.s: We tend to forget that sea level is a product of technically and culturally determined assumptions.
ex.t: 我们往往忘记，海平面其实是由技术和文化因素决定的一系列假设的产物。

ex.s: In this book, I tell a story of these assumptions.
ex.t: 在本书中，我将讲述这些假设的故事。

ex.s: Appropriately, the book took shape during a summer spent between sea and mountains.
ex.t: 巧的是，这本书是在一个往来于大海与群山之间的夏天逐渐成形的。

ex.s: Little do they know that as they do so, a burst of energy is sent up to street level to help charge an electric car.

ex.s: Barcelona has put together a package of clean energy technologies to help public transportation go greener, while also doing its part to tackle climate change and aid Europe’s difficult shift to the privately owned electric vehicle market.
ex.t: 巴塞罗那整合了一整套清洁能源技术，帮助公共交通变得更加环保，同时也为应对气候变化尽一份力，并助力欧洲向私人电动汽车市场的艰难转型。

ex.s: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
ex.t: “我感到惊喜，因为我总是在找哪里能给它充电，”Espinoza在巴塞罗那南部一个工薪阶层社区乘地铁前说。

ex.s: They consist of an electric motor which collects energy used in the braking action that would be lost as heat by conventional brakes.

ex.s: Alvaro Luna, a professor of electrical engineering, said that the system is innovative in so far as it allows for recycled energy to be redirected to specific local uses — in this case powering electric cars parked nearby.
ex.t: 电气工程教授Alvaro Luna表示，该系统的创新之处在于，它能把回收的能量重新导向特定的本地用途——在这个案例中就是为停放在附近的电动汽车供电。

ex.s: The study used a dataset of 1,600 reviews of Chicago hotels.
ex.t: 该研究使用了一个包含1600条芝加哥酒店评论的数据集。

ex.s: Each subject got eight reviews to read: a balanced set of two positive fake, two positive real, two negative fake and two negative real, presented in a random order.
ex.t: 每名受试者读到8条评论：两条正面虚假、两条正面真实、两条负面虚假、两条负面真实，均衡搭配并随机排序。

ex.s: When a negative review is fake, we get tricked,” Azimi says.
ex.t: 当一条负面评论是假的时候，我们就上当受骗了，”Azimi说。

ex.s: When it came to faking a review, length was important to believability, as was detail.
ex.t: 在伪造评论时，篇幅对可信度很重要，细节也是如此。

ex.s: A long, negative review of a hotel, complete with lots of information, tended to convince participants.
ex.t: 一条内容翔实的长篇酒店负面评论往往能取信于参与者。

ex.s: A lengthy, positive review, on the other hand, was regarded as suspicious, and participants tended to trust writers that kept their glowing reviews short.

ex.s: While he held the notion that objective reality exists, he said our mind plays a necessary role in structuring and shaping our perceptions.
ex.t: 虽然他坚持认为客观现实存在，但他说我们的心灵在构建和塑造我们的感知方面起着必要的作用。

ex.s: So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation.
ex.t: 所以，如果我们接受宇宙是不可知的，我们也接受我们永远无法知道自己是否生活在计算机模拟中。

ex.s: And then, we can shift our inquiry from “Is the universe a computer simulation? ” to “Can we model the universe as a computer simulation? ” Modelling reality is what we do.
ex.t: 然后，我们可以将探究从"宇宙是计算机模拟吗？"转向"我们能将宇宙建模为计算机模拟吗？"对现实进行建模正是我们所做的。

ex.s: In Newton’s era, we imagined the universe as a clock.
ex.t: 在牛顿时代，我们把宇宙想象成一座时钟。

ex.s: There is no point in arguing if the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation.
ex.t: 争论宇宙是一座时钟、一组粒子还是计算的产物是没有意义的。

ex.s: It can be imagined that comparable to the process of building previous scientific models, developing the “computer simulation” metaphor-based model will also be a hugely rewarding exercise.
ex.t: 可以想象，与建立以往科学模型的过程类似，开发基于"计算机模拟"隐喻的模型也将是一项非常有价值的练习。

ex.s: The similarity of moral virtues across cultures is striking, even though the relative ranking of the virtues may vary with a social group’s history and environment.
ex.t: 不同文化间道德美德的相似性令人瞩目，尽管美德的相对排名可能因社会群体的历史和环境而异。

ex.s: More generally, social instincts motivate us to learn how to behave in a socially complex world.
ex.t: 更广泛地说，社会本能促使我们学习如何在复杂的社会环境中行事。

ex.s: The mechanism involves a repurposed reward system originally used to develop habits important for self-care.
ex.t: 这一机制涉及一个重新利用的奖励系统，该系统原本用于培养对自我照顾重要的习惯。

ex.s: Good social habits do something similar in a social context.
ex.t: 良好的社会习惯在社会环境中起到类似的作用。

ex.s: We learn to tell the truth, even when lying is self-serving; we help a grandparent even when it is inconvenient.
ex.t: 我们学会说实话，即使撒谎对自己有利；我们在不方便的时候也会帮助祖父母。

ex.s: We acquire what we call a sense of right and wrong.
ex.t: 我们获得了所谓的是非感。

ex.s: In humans, a greatly enlarged brain boosts self-control, just as it boosts problem-solving skills in the social as well as the physical world.
ex.t: 在人类中，大大扩容的大脑增强了自控能力，正如它增强了社交世界和物理世界中的解决问题能力一样。

ex.s: According to Isaiah Berlin, the hedgehog knows one thing very well, and the fox knows a lot of things.
ex.t: 根据以赛亚·伯林的说法，刺猬非常了解一件事，而狐狸了解很多事情。

ex.s: Is there a clear advantage of one style over the other?
ex.t: 一种风格比另一种风格有明显优势吗？

ex.s: The advantage that foxes have is that they are more likely to seek out new information from a broader range of sources, and are comfortable with uncertainty and new information. ___38___ They try to include it in their viewpoint rather than to exclude it from their thinking.
ex.t: 狐狸的优势在于它们更有可能从更广泛的来源寻找新信息，并且对不确定性和新信息感到适应。___38___它们试图将其纳入自己的观点，而不是排除在思考之外。

ex.s: They also have a clearer estimation of what they know and don’t know.
ex.t: 他们也对自己知道什么和不知道什么有更清晰的估计。

ex.s: The question can be answered in a foxy hedgehog style. ___39___ The choice between being a hedgehog or a fox is a false trade-off.
ex.t: 这个问题可以用狐狸式的刺猬方式来回答。___39___在刺猬和狐狸之间做选择是一个错误的权衡。

ex.s: But there can be a downside to concentration on one big thing.
ex.t: 但专注于一件事也可能有缺点。

ex.s: When I decided to pursue a postgraduate degree, I wanted to develop a novel research programme and quickly establish myself as an independent scientist.
ex.t: 当我决定攻读研究生学位时，我想开发一个新的研究计划，并迅速确立自己作为独立科学家的地位。

ex.s: As a result, the first four years of my postgraduate career were defined by a series of failures.
ex.t: 结果，我研究生生涯的前四年以一系列失败为特征。

ex.s: Finally, I conducted an elegant experiment that would not have been possible without the help of the members in the lab.
ex.t: 最终，我完成了一个优雅的实验，如果没有实验室成员的帮助，这是不可能的。

ex.s: My adviser saw this experience as a groundbreaking success, emphasising the collaborating skills I acquired.
ex.t: 我的导师将这次经历视为突破性的成功，强调我所获得的协作技能。

ex.s: A few months later, when I repeated the experiment in my home lab, I produced more publishable data.
ex.t: 几个月后，当我在自己的实验室重复这个实验时，我产出了更多可发表的数据。

ex.s: By learning when to ask for help, I eventually found myself on the way to becoming an independent scientist.
ex.t: 通过学会何时寻求帮助，我终于踏上了成为独立科学家的道路。

ex.s: > The adviser considered the author’s experience in the lab a groundbreaking success because publishable data had been produced.
ex.t: 导师认为作者在实验室的经历是一次突破性的成功，因为产生了可发表的数据。

ex.s: When John Todd was a child he loved to explore the woods around his house, observing how nature solved problems.
ex.t: 当约翰·托德还是个孩子的时候，他喜欢探索房子周围的树林，观察大自然如何解决问题。

ex.s: A dirty stream, for example, often became clear after flowing through plants and along rocks where tiny creatures lived.
ex.t: 例如，一条肮脏的小溪流经植物和居住着微小生物的岩石后常常变清澈。

ex.s: He decided to build what he would later call an eco-machine.
ex.t: 他决定建造他后来称之为"生态机器"的东西。

ex.s: First, he constructed a series of clear fiberglass tanks connected to each other.
ex.t: 首先，他建造了一系列相互连接的透明玻璃纤维水箱。

ex.s: After a few weeks, John added the sludge.
ex.t: 几周后，约翰加入了污泥。

ex.s: He also designed an eco-machine to clean canal water in Fuzhou, a city in southeast China.
ex.t: 他还设计了一台生态机器来清理中国东南部城市福州的运河水。

ex.s: “Life on Earth is kind of a box of spare parts for the inventor,” he says.
ex.t: “地球上的生命对发明家来说就像一盒备用零件，”他说。

ex.s: He had an inquiring mind.
ex.t: 他有求知若渴的头脑。

ex.s: He longed to be a doctor.
ex.t: 他渴望成为一名医生。

ex.s: To build an ecosystem.

ex.s: To show an application of John’s idea.
ex.t: 为了展示约翰理念的一个应用。

ex.s: The goal of this book is to make the case for digital minimalism, including a detailed exploration of what it asks and why it works, and then to teach you how to adopt this philosophy if you decide it’s right for you.
ex.t: 本书旨在阐明数字极简主义的主张，包括详细探讨它的要求以及它为何有效，然后教你在认为它适合你的情况下如何践行这一理念。

ex.s: In part one, I describe the philosophical foundations of digital minimalism, starting with an examination of the forces that are making so many people’s digital lives increasingly intolerable, before moving on to a detailed discussion of the digital minimalism philosophy.
ex.t: 在第一部分中，我阐述了数字极简主义的哲学基础，首先审视了使许多人的数字生活日益难以忍受的各种力量，然后详细讨论了数字极简主义哲学。

ex.s: At the end of the thirty days, you will then add back a small number of carefully chosen online activities that you believe will provide massive benefits to the things you value.
ex.t: 三十天结束时，你再重新加入少量经过精心挑选的线上活动，即那些你认为能为你所珍视的事情带来巨大益处的活动。

ex.s: In doing so, I’ll draw on an experiment I ran in 2018 in which over 1,600 people agreed to perform a digital declutter.
ex.t: 在此过程中，我将引用我在2018年进行的一项实验，其中有1600多人同意进行数字清理。

ex.s: Each chapter concludes with a collection of practices, which are designed to help you act on the big ideas of the chapter.
ex.t: 每一章都以一组实践练习结尾，这些练习旨在帮助你把本章的重要观点付诸行动。

ex.s: You can view these practices as a toolbox meant to aid your efforts to build a minimalist lifestyle that words for your particular circumstances.
ex.t: 你可以把这些实践看作一个工具箱，用来帮助你建立一种适合自己具体情况的极简生活方式。

ex.s: Advocating a simple digital lifestyle.
ex.t: 倡导一种简单的数字生活方式。

ex.s: Promoting the use of a digital device.
ex.t: 推广数字设备的使用。

ex.s: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the “wisdom of crowds” effect.
ex.t: 1907年3月7日，英国统计学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐述了后来被称为“群体智慧”效应的现象。

ex.s: The experiment of estimation he conducted showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate.
ex.t: 他进行的估算实验表明，在某些情况下，大量独立估算的平均值可以相当准确。

ex.s: When enough of these errors are averaged together, they cancel each other out, resulting in a more accurate estimate.
ex.t: 当足够多的这类错误被平均在一起时，它们会相互抵消，从而得出更准确的估算。

ex.s: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.
ex.t: 该研究的关键发现是：当人群被进一步分成可以进行讨论的小组时，这些小组的平均值比同等数量的独立个体的平均值更准确。

ex.s: In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion.
ex.t: 在一项有100名大学生参加的后续研究中，研究人员试图更好地了解小组成员在讨论中实际做了什么。

ex.s: Most frequently, the groups reported that they “shared arguments and reasoned together.” Somehow, these arguments and reasoning resulted in a global reduction in error.
ex.t: 最常见的是，各小组报告说他们“分享论点并一起推理”。不知何故，这些论点和推理使错误总体上减少了。

ex.s: Taking responsibility for mistakes is a positive step, but don’t beat yourself up about them.
ex.t: 为错误承担责任是积极的一步，但不要因此过分自责。

ex.s: In a journal or on a piece of paper, put the heading “Personal strengths.” ____17____ Are you caring?
ex.t: 在日记本上或一张纸上写下标题“个人优点”。____17____ 你体贴吗？

ex.s: A good listener?
ex.t: 你是个好的倾听者吗？

ex.s: At the top of a second page, put the heading “Acts of kindness.” On this one, list all the positive things you’ve done for others.
ex.t: 在第二页的顶部写下标题“善举”。在这一页上，列出你为他人做过的所有积极的事情。

ex.s: It might be the time when you helped a friend with their homework, when you did the ironing without being asked, or when you baked cookies after the family had had a tiring day. ____18____
ex.t: 可能是你帮朋友做功课的时候，可能是你主动熨衣服的时候，也可能是你在家人疲惫一天后烤饼干的时候。____18____

ex.s: You could ask a friend or family member to help add to your list. ____19____ That way, you could exchange thoughts on what makes each of you special and the aspects of your personality that shine through.
ex.t: 你可以请朋友或家人帮你补充这个清单。____19____ 这样，你们就可以交流想法，谈谈是什么让彼此与众不同，以及你们性格中闪光的方面。

ex.s: In fact, don’t wait until you’ve made a mistake to try this — it’s a great way to boost self-confidence at any time.
ex.t: 事实上，不要等到犯了错误才尝试这样做——这在任何时候都是增强自信的好方法。

ex.s: The thing is, it’s true. ____20____ We’ re all changing and learning all the time and mistakes are a positive way to develop and grow.
ex.t: 问题是，这是真的。____20____ 我们一直在改变和学习，而错误是发展和成长的积极方式。

ex.s: A little self-forgiveness also goes a long way.
ex.t: 一点自我宽恕也大有裨益。

ex.s: Whatever the mistake, remember it isn’t a fixed aspect of your personality.
ex.t: 无论是什么错误，请记住它并不是你性格中固定不变的一部分。

ex.s: Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers is a celebration of an everyday object — the book, represented here in almost three hundred artworks from museums around the world.
ex.t: 《阅读的艺术：爱书人的艺术》是对一种日常物品——书的礼赞，书中汇集了近三百件来自世界各地博物馆的艺术作品来呈现它。

ex.s: In this “book of books,” artworks are selected and arranged in a way that emphasizes these connections between different eras and cultures.
ex.t: 在这本“书中的书”里，艺术作品的挑选和编排方式突出了不同时代和文化之间的这些联系。

ex.s: We see scenes of children learning to read at home or at school, with the book as a focus for relations between the generations.
ex.t: 我们看到孩子们在家中或学校学习阅读的场景，书本成为几代人之间关系的焦点。

ex.s: From a 21st-century point of view, the printed book is certainly ancient, but it remains as interactive as any battery-powered e-reader.
ex.t: 从21世纪的视角看，印刷书当然古老，但它与任何电池供电的电子阅读器一样具有互动性。

ex.s: To serve its function, a book must be activated by a user: the cover opened, the pages parted, the contents reviewed, perhaps notes written down or words underlined.
ex.t: 为了发挥其功能，一本书必须由使用者来激活：打开封面，翻开书页，浏览内容，也许还要写下笔记或划出字句。

ex.s: And in contrast to our increasingly networked lives where the information we consume is monitored and tracked, a printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, “off-line” activity.
ex.t: 而且，与我们日益网络化的生活——我们所消费的信息受到监控和追踪——形成对比的是，印刷书仍然提供了一种完全私密的、“离线”活动的机会。

ex.s: If you’re lucky, there might be a pocket park near where you live, but it’s unusual to find places in a city that are relatively wild.
ex.t: 如果运气好，你住的地方附近可能有一个口袋公园，但在城市里找到相对自然野性的地方是很少见的。

ex.s: Past research has found health and wellness benefits of nature for humans, but a new study shows that wildness in urban areas is extremely important for human well-being.
ex.t: 过去的研究发现了大自然对人类健康和幸福的益处，而一项新研究表明，城市中的自然野趣对人类的幸福极其重要。

ex.s: The research team focused on a large urban park.
ex.t: 研究团队聚焦于一大型城市公园。

ex.s: They surveyed several hundred park-goers, asking them to submit a written summary online of a meaningful interaction they had with nature in the park.
ex.t: 他们调查了数百名游园者，请他们在线提交一份书面小结，描述他们在公园中与自然进行的一次有意义的互动。

ex.s: For example, one participant’s experience of “We sat and listened to the waves at the beach for a while” was assigned the categories “sitting at beach” and “listening to waves.”
ex.t: 例如，一位参与者的经历“我们在海滩上坐着听了一会儿海浪”被归入“坐在海滩上”和“听海浪”两个类别。

ex.s: Across the 320 submissions, a pattern of categories the researchers call a “nature language” began to emerge.
ex.t: 在320份提交材料中，一种被研究人员称为“自然语言”的类别模式开始显现。

ex.s: After the coding of all submissions, half a dozen categories were noted most often as important to visitors.
ex.t: 对所有提交材料进行编码后，有六种类别最常被游客提及为重要。

ex.s: These include encountering wildlife, walking along the edge of water, and following an established trail.
ex.t: 这些类别包括遇见野生动物、沿着水边散步，以及沿着既有的小径行走。

ex.s: Naming each nature experience creates a usable language, which helps people recognize and take part in the activities that are most satisfying and meaningful to them.
ex.t: 为每种自然体验命名创造出一种可用的语言，帮助人们认识并参与那些对他们来说最令人满足、最有意义的活动。

ex.s: For example, the experience of walking along the edge of water might be satisfying for a young professional on a weekend hike in the park.
ex.t: 例如，沿着水边散步的体验，对一位周末在公园里徒步的年轻职场人士来说可能很令人满足。

ex.s: Back downtown during a workday, they can enjoy a more domestic form of this interaction by walking along a fountain on their lunch break.
ex.t: 回到市中心的上班日，他们可以在午休时间沿着喷泉散步，享受这种互动的一种更居家化的形式。

ex.s: “We’re trying to generate a language that helps bring the human-nature interactions back into our daily lives.
ex.t: “我们正试图创造一种语言，帮助把人与自然的互动带回我们的日常生活。

ex.s: And for that to happen, we also need to protect nature so that we can interact with it,” said Peter Kahn, a senior author of the study.
ex.t: 要做到这一点，我们还需要保护自然，这样我们才能与它互动，”该研究的资深作者彼得·卡恩说。

ex.s: As an artist who shares her journey on social media, I’m often asked by curious followers how to begin an art journey.

ex.s: So I’ve put together some good tips for starting an art journey.
ex.t: 所以我整理了一些开启艺术之旅的好建议。

ex.s: By the early 1970s, after centuries of cruel and continuous hunting by settlers, 600 to 800 grizzlies remained on a mere 2 percent of their former range in the Northern Rockies.

ex.s: If you want to tell the history of the whole world, a history that does not privilege one part of humanity, you cannot do it through texts alone, because only some of the world has ever had texts, while most of the world, for most of the time, has not.
ex.t: 如果你想讲述整个世界的历史，一部不偏袒任何一部分人类的历史，你就不能只依靠文字文献，因为世界上只有一部分地区曾经有过文字，而世界上大部分地区在大部分时间里都没有。

ex.s: Ideally a history would bring together texts and objects, and some chapters of this book are able to do just that, but in many cases we simply can’t.
ex.t: 理想情况下，一部历史应该把文字和实物结合起来，本书的某些章节能够做到这一点，但在许多情况下我们根本做不到。

ex.s: From the Australian side, we have only a wooden shield (盾) dropped by a man in flight after his first experience of gunshot.

ex.s: The Caribbean Taino, the Australian Aboriginals, the African people of Benin and the Incas, all of whom appear in this book, can speak to us now of their past achievements most powerfully through the objects they made: a history told through things gives them back a voice.
ex.t: 加勒比海的泰诺人、澳大利亚原住民、贝宁的非洲人和印加人——他们都出现在本书中——如今可以通过他们制作的物品最有力地向我们讲述他们过去的成就：一部通过实物讲述的历史把声音还给了他们。

ex.t: 不过在这个过程中我也学到了一些东西，希望如果你也在尽力想办法在一个不太支持的家庭环境中做出改变，这些经验能给你带来鼓励。

ex.s: A few days later, I came back with my first jars of zero waste groceries, and my dad commented on how silly it was for me to carry jars everywhere.
ex.t: 几天后，我带着第一批零浪费罐装杂货回来，我爸爸评论说我到处带罐子多傻啊。

ex.t: 正如西北大学电气工程和计算机科学教授克里斯蒂安·哈蒙德所说："系统从来没有一个阶段知道自己谈论的是什么。"

ex.s: A computer works with symbols.
ex.t: 计算机处理符号。

ex.s: Its program specifies a set of rules to transform one string of symbols into another.
ex.t: 其程序指定了一套规则，将一个符号串转换为另一个符号串。

ex.s: Indeed, to a computer, meaning is irrelevant.
ex.t: 事实上，对于计算机来说，意义无关紧要。

ex.s: What matters is not just the outside of a string of symbols, but the inside too, not just how they are arranged but what they mean.
ex.t: 重要的不仅是符号串的外表，还有内在；不仅是它们的排列方式，还有它们的含义。

ex.s: Meaning emerges through a process of social interaction, not of computation, interaction that shapes the content of the symbols in our heads.
ex.t: 意义通过社会互动的过程产生，而非计算过程——这种互动塑造了我们头脑中符号的内容。

ex.s: In a world where nearly 800 million people a year go hungry, “food waste goes against the moral grain,” as Elizabeth Royte writes in this month’s cover story.

ex.s: That makes food waste an environmental problem.

ex.s: For almost a year I struggled on, constantly staring at this wall that faced me.
ex.t: 近一年来我一直在挣扎， constantly 盯着面前的那堵墙。

ex.s: One day, I attended a presentation by wildlife conservationist Grant Brown at my high school.
ex.t: 有一天，我在高中参加了野生动物保护学家Grant Brown的演讲。

ex.s: His presentation not only awed and inspired me, but also helped emerge an inner desire to make a difference in the world.
ex.t: 他的演讲不仅让我惊叹和受到启发，还激发了我内心想要在这个世界做出改变的愿望。

ex.s: I joined a pre-presentation dinner with him and that smaller setting allowed me to slowly build up my courage to speak one-on-one with him—an idea that had seemed completely impossible.
ex.t: 我参加了演讲前的晚宴，那个较小的场合让我慢慢建立起勇气与他一对一交流——这个想法曾经看起来完全不可能。

ex.s: A month later, Brown invited me to attend the World Youth Wildlife Conference.
ex.t: 一个月后，Brown邀请我参加世界青年野生动物大会。

ex.s: Looking back, I now see that this would be the first in a series of timely opportunities that my old self would have let pass, but that this new and more confident Alice enthusiastically seized.
ex.t: 回顾往事，我现在明白这将是第一个及时机会，旧的我可能会让它溜走，而这个新的、更自信的Alice热情地抓住了。

ex.s: I decided to commit to completing the applications, and soon I was a part of a growing global team of young people working to protect nature.
ex.t: 我决定致力于完成申请，很快我就成为了一个不断壮大的全球青年保护自然团队的一员。

ex.s: Patience is a cure of anxiety.
ex.t: 耐心是焦虑的良药。

ex.s: “What would the world be if there were no hunger?” It’s a question that Professor Crystal would ask her students.
ex.t: "如果没有饥饿，世界会是什么样？"这是Crystal教授会问她学生的问题。

ex.s: They found it hard to answer, she wrote later, because imagining something that isn’t part of real life—and learning how to make it real—is a rare skill.
ex.t: 她后来写道，他们发现这个问题很难回答，因为想象一些不是现实生活的一部分的事情——以及学习如何使其成为现实——是一种罕见的技能。

ex.s: Crystal set out to change that, and helped to create a global movement.
ex.t: Crystal着手改变这一点，并帮助创建了一个全球运动。

ex.s: The result—an approach known as systems thinking—is now seen as essential in meeting global challenges.
ex.t: 其结果——一种被称为系统思维的方法——现在被认为对于应对全球挑战至关重要。

ex.s: A systems approach to creating change is also built on the assumption that everyone in the system has equal power.
ex.t: 创建变化的系统方法还建立在这样的假设之上：系统中的每个人都拥有同等的权力。

ex.s: But as some researchers find, the food system is not an equal one.
ex.t: 但正如一些研究人员发现的，食物系统并不是一个平等的体系。

ex.s: More researchers, policymakers and representatives from the food industry must learn to look beyond their direct lines of responsibility and adopt a systems approach.
ex.t: 更多研究人员、政策制定者和食品行业代表必须学会超越其直接责任范围，采用系统思维的方法。

ex.s: This allows it to take in air at 30 times the speed of a human sneeze, enabling it to drink 3L of water a second.
ex.t: 这使它能以人类打喷嚏速度的30倍吸气，每秒能喝下3升水。

ex.s: Dogs may indeed be able to distinguish between happy and angry human faces, according to a new study.

ex.s: The researchers found that the dogs were able to pick the angry or happy face by touching a picture of it with their noses more often than one would expect by random chance.
ex.t: "我们可以排除狗只是根据简单线索如牙齿的外观来区分图片的可能性，"研究作者科辛·穆勒说。

ex.s: "We can rule out that the dogs simply distinguish between the pictures based on a simple cue, such as the sight of teeth," said study author Corsin Muller.
ex.t: "通过我们的研究我们认为我们现在可以有信心地得出结论至少一些狗能够识别人类面部表情，"穆勒告诉Live Science。

ex.s: "Instead, our results suggest that the successful dogs realized that a smiling mouth means the same thing as smiling eyes, and the same rule applies to an angry mouth having the same meaning as angry eyes.”
ex.t: 此时还不清楚狗为什么似乎具备识别人类不同面部表情的能力。

ex.s: "To us, the most likely explanation appears to be that the basis lies in their living with humans, which gives them a lot of exposure to human facial expressions," and this exposure has provided them with many chances to learn to distinguish between them, Muller said.

ex.s: Recently，I conceptualized a new approach to timekeeping that's connected to circumstances on our planet，conditions that might change as a result of global warming．We're now building a clock at the Anchorage Museum that reflects the total flow of several major Alaskan rivers，which are sensitive to local and global environmental changes．We've programmed it to match an atomic clock if the waterways continue to flow at their present rate．If the rivers run faster in the future on average，the clock will get ahead of standard time．If they run slower，you'll see the opposite effect．

ex.s: The term “budget line” has several related meanings, including a couple that are self- evident and a third that is not.

ex.s: The budget line as an Informal Consumer Understanding
ex.t: 非正式地说，预算线描述了给定预算和特定商品的可承受能力边界。

ex.s: The budget line is an elementary concept that most consumers understand intuitively without a need for graphs and equations — it's the household budget, for example.
ex.t: 给定有限金额的钱，消费者只能花费相同金额购买商品。

ex.s: Taken informally, the budget line describes the boundary of affordability for a given budget and specific goods.
ex.t: 如果消费者有X金额的钱并且想购买两种商品A和B，她只能购买总计X的商品。

ex.s: Given a limited amount of money, a consumer can only spend that same amount buying goods.
ex.t: 如果消费者需要数量为A的商品花费0.75，那么她只能在购买B时花费剩余的0.25X。

ex.s: If the consumer has X amount of money and wants to buy two goods A and B, she can only purchase goods totaling X.
ex.t: 这似乎太显而易见了以至于不值得写下来或阅读。

ex.s: If the consumer needs an amount of A costing 0.75, she can then spend only 0.25 X, the amount remaining, on her purchase of B.
ex.t: 然而，事实证明，这个概念——大多数消费者每天都会多次做出这个决定而不需要思考——是经济学中更正式的预算线概念的基础，下文将对此进行解释。

ex.s: Lines in a Budget
ex.t: 这实际上是一张未来支出的地图，其中所有组成部分的支出都被单独注明和量化。

ex.s: This is effectively a map of future expenditures, with all the constituent expenditures individually noted and quantified.
ex.t: 作为经济学概念的预算线

ex.s: There' s nothing very complicated about this usage, a budget line is one of the lines in the budget, with the service or good to be purchased named and the cost quantified,
ex.t: 经济学研究与人类一般行为的关系的一个有趣方式是，许多经济理论是上述简单概念的正式化——消费者对自己拥有的金额以及这笔金额能买到什么的非正式理解。
